questions.q: A new teammate asks the agent how checkout works in an unfamiliar 900-file repository. The agent starts by reading every file and reaches 70% of its context before it has answered. Which approach is better?
opts: Grep for entry points first, then Read the hits and follow imports.
Glob every source file and read them all in alphabetical order, summarising each one as it goes.
Concatenate the whole repository into one very large file and read that file in a single pass.
Switch to a model with a larger context window and keep on reading every single file first.
questions.explain: Understanding is built step by step: search to locate where the flow starts, then read only what the trail leads to (guide TS 2.5, skill 4). B, C and D all still read everything up front, only more neatly or with a bigger window.

questions.q: The agent must find every use of a payments helper that application code reaches through a wrapper module. The wrapper re-exports it under other names (`pay_charge`, `pay_refund`). A search for the helper's original name finds only 2 of about 40 usages. What should the agent do?
opts: Search again for the original name using different regular-expression flags and case settings.
Search for the wrapper's file name and assume that every importer of it uses the helper.
Read the wrapper to list its exported names, then search the codebase for each name.
Glob for files with ‘pay’ in their names and read all of the files that come back in full.
questions.explain: Callers use the exported names, not the original one. List what the wrapper exports first, then search for each exported name (guide TS 2.5, skill 5). A repeats a search that cannot match; B counts importers rather than usages; D matches file names, which says nothing about who calls what.
